channel.title: Blocktape
channel.description: Blocktape reports crypto news: exchange and market moves, protocol upgrades, token launches, security incidents, regulation and enforcement across chains.

item.title: Wrapped XMR Adds Public-Chain Visibility to Monero
item.description: Wrapped XMR carries Monero onto another blockchain, where token activity may be public even as native XMR stays private, with bridge and redemption risks.

item.title: Monero’s Two-Minute Blocks Set the Starting Point for XMR Bridge Waits
item.description: Estimate an XMR bridge wait by separating Monero block inclusion, the service’s confirmation threshold, swap processing and destination-chain settlement.

item.title: Bridged tokens can keep transfer restrictions across chains
item.description: Bridged tokens retain transfer limits when destination contracts enforce the same rules; check token code, admin controls and bridge design before moving funds.

item.title: Polygon PoS withdrawal proofs have no fixed gas cost
item.description: A bridge proof has no fixed gas price: the Ethereum claim costs depend on proof execution, calldata and block fees, while proof generation itself is off-chain.

item.title: Transfer-tax tokens need bridge support for net amounts
item.description: Transfer-tax tokens cross chains reliably only when a bridge supports their net received amount; check token support, test a small transfer, and verify settlement.

item.title: Polygon Bridge routes: what regular users should compare
item.description: Use Polygon Bridge for routine Ethereum–Polygon transfers when a direct route suits the job, and compare alternatives by route design, cost and withdrawal time.

item.title: Failed Cross-Chain Messages: Check the State Before Retrying
item.description: A failed bridge or cross-chain call may be pending, verified, or reverted on arrival; check its stage and cause before resubmitting to avoid duplicate actions.

item.title: How to Arrive on a New Chain With Gas to Spend
item.description: A cross-chain token transfer can arrive without the native coin needed for the next transaction; plan a gas drop, separate top-up or sponsored call before sending.

item.title: Destination gas drops add spendable funds after a bridge
item.description: Destination gas drops send a small balance of a chain’s native token with a cross-chain transfer, letting recipients make a follow-up transaction without arranging a separate top-up.

item.title: How to check a crypto bridge route for phishing
item.description: Bridge phishing often starts before a wallet prompt: verify the site, chains, token, route contracts and approval details before signing or sending funds.

item.title: How to Check Whether a Cross-Chain Transfer Arrived
item.description: Check a cross-chain transfer on its destination chain: match the transaction or balance to the intended network, token and recipient.

item.title: Low-liquidity BSC charts can magnify small trades
item.description: Low-liquidity BSC charts can move on small trades; compare pool reserves, executed volume and trade size before treating a candle as a lasting price signal.

item.title: How Poocoin Charts and Swaps BNB Smart Chain Tokens
item.description: Poocoin combines BNB Smart Chain token charts, wallet tracking and a built-in swap; check a token’s contract and trade details before deciding to swap.

item.title: Browser wallet choice starts with the account behind each bridge transfer
item.description: Choose a browser wallet by how it handles accounts, networks and recovery; check the same address before signing each bridge step, including later claims.

item.title: Contract Wallets Change How Users Authorize Bridge Transfers
item.description: Contract wallets replace one-key authorization with on-chain rules; bridge transfers still depend on destination support, account deployment and gas on both networks at each step.

item.title: What a Merkle Proof Checks Before a Crypto Withdrawal
item.description: A Merkle proof confirms that a withdrawal record is included in a committed batch, but it cannot finalize the batch or replace the bridge’s claim and fee steps.

item.title: Bridge transfers need gas on both sides of the transaction
item.description: A bridge transfer can require gas on both networks: estimate the source transaction, keep native tokens for later steps, and verify what the quote includes.

item.title: Manta Pacific Withdrawals Still Depend on Ethereum Finality
item.description: Manta Pacific withdrawals settle through an Ethereum proof, a challenge window and a final transaction; Manta’s fast-finality plan changes the wait after rollout.

item.title: Cross-chain deposit channels can preserve access after vault changes
item.description: Cross-chain deposit channels can outlive vault changes, but their time limits still matter; learn how address reuse, key handovers and expiry affect late funds.

item.title: Treasury should reconcile Chainflip swaps from deposit to payout
item.description: Treasury should match each Chainflip source deposit to its destination payout, record fees and execution value separately, and keep failed or partial swaps open.
